jobs.occupation: DIAS Fellow in Hybrid War and Democratic Challenges
jobs.description:
The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Digital Democracy Centre (DDC) at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) seek an outstanding candidate to fill a tenure track Fellow (Assistant Professor level) position with a background in computational social sciences, data science, including (but not limited to) computer science, communication, political science, linguistics, information studies, digital humanities, sociology or psychology on the topic of Hybrid War and Democratic Challenges. The candidate is expected to start on April 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The place of employment will be Odense.

The ’Hybrid War and Democracy’ initiative explores changes in how international conflicts are waged. Domestic and foreign influence campaigns are bolstered by new digital technologies and artificial intelligence. This creates new challenges for democracies, threat perceptions, information integrity, and for citizens’ information agency.

We are looking for a researcher with clear potential for research excellence who thrives in and is inspired by interdisciplinary collaboration. The ideal candidate will be expected to contribute to high-quality research in their field while embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven inquiry and interdisciplinary dialogue. The successful candidate should have a strong and promising research profile, with potential for attracting external research funding, and a demonstrated ability to work across disciplines. The candidate will be attached to both the DDC and DIAS and should be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU. Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard assistant professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research and leadership activities.

The ideal candidate should demonstrate: 

• 
A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue.

• 
A strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration, contributing to research that bridges multiple fields. 

• 
Strong interest in driving internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

• 
Engagement in various forms of research dissemination, including interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

• 
Ability to communicate project results in English both in writing in academic contexts and to the broader public.

• 
Ability of working independently and on a team through research process, including data collection, data analysis, writing scientific articles, and knowledge dissemination.

• 
Ability (preferably) to work with computational methods.

Qualifications

Successful applicants must: 

• 
Hold a PhD or similar qualifications within relevant fields of computational social sciences, data science, including (but not limited to) computer science, communication, political science, linguistics, information studies, digital humanities, sociology or psychology. 

• 
To qualify for the position as Assistant Professor you must have obtained (or approved to defend) a PhD or similar degree by the application deadline. 

• 
Exhibit curiosity-driven research excellence, thinking beyond traditional boundaries. 

• 
Be fluent in English.

• 
Show potential for attracting external research funding. Experience in applying for external funding and a strong international network, are considered comparative advantages.

• 
Have research publications that demonstrate their excellence and broad thinking. 

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally. 

About the DDC

The DDC is a part of the Faculty of Social Sciences. It is an interdisciplinary Centre with members from computer science, law, media studies, political science, business, and organizations. The DDC believes in fostering a stimulating and inspiring environment for both faculty members and students. The DDC’s ambition is to recruit, develop, and retain talented scholars committed to both research, education, and impact. Furthermore, the DDC wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

Additional information

For further information about being a fellow at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email (director-dias@sdu.dk).

For more questions about the position please contact Prof Claes de Vreese via email (chv@sam.sdu.dk).

Application, salary, and employment terms

The position is based at the DDC and DIAS in Odense and includes regular participation in DIAS and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Employment is governed by the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

The salary comprises a seniority-based base salary and a centrally agreed supplement.

Additional supplements may be negotiated locally.

As of 1 August 2026, the annual salary for an Assistant Professor is DKK 480,224.96 (salary level 6), consisting of a base salary of DKK 417,456 and a supplement of DKK 62,768.96.

All amounts are stated before tax, before added pension (18.07%), and any additional supplements. Pension contributions are paid by SDU, and both salary components (the annual salary and the supplement) are pensionable. For further information, please see SDU’s pages on salary, taxation, and general employment conditions.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

Danish Tenure Track Programme

An appointment as Assistant Professor (Danish tenure track) is limited to a six-year term. The academic assessment for promotion to Associate Professor must be initiated no later than the end of the fifth year of employment. However, a tenure track assistant professor may request an earlier assessment within the first four years.

If the initial assessment is negative, one reassessment may be conducted during the final six months prior to a potential transition. A maximum of two assessments may be undertaken.

A positive assessment leads to appointment to a permanent Associate Professor position. If the final assessment is negative, the employment may be terminated in accordance with the applicable collective agreement.

A six-year development plan for the tenure track programme is established at the start of employment.

Application requirements
The application must include the following:

• 
Letter of motivation that clearly explains the applicant's interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position.

• 
Detailed CV including documentation of experience, and contacts for possible references. 

• 
An elaborated research and funding plan (max 4 pages) for the next three years including a description of synergy with the department's activities and the potential to benefit from DIAS’s interdisciplinary environment.

• 
Copies of certificates/Diplomas (Master and PhD degree).

• 
Complete list of publications, indicating which publications are most relevant for the position.

• 
Up to 3 of the most relevant research articles – if you submit a monograph, it counts as 3 articles. Please upload one PDF file for each publication. For co-authored publications, briefly describe the extent of the co-authorship or your contribution to the publications (please do this for each co-authored publication). You can do so by using this form or by describing the co-authorship in such a way that the committee can assess the extent of your contribution.

• 
Applicants are requested to submit a teaching portfolio with the application as documentation for teaching experience as well as supervision qualifications. Formal application instructions and a guide for the teaching portfolio can be found here.

All application materials must be submitted in English, and only applications written in English will be considered.

We recommend that international applicants take the time to visit websites of Work in Denmark and the International Staff Office at SDU. Here you can find information and facts about moving to, working and living in Denmark.

Submission guidelines

• 
Files must be submitted in PDF format.

• 
If multiple files are needed for a single section, combine them into one PDF file.

• 
Zip files, image files (jpg, png, etc.), and password-protected PDF files will not be accepted. All PDF files must be unlocked to allow binding.

• 
Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

Assessment

Shortlisting may be used as part of the assessment process. Read about shortlisting at SDU.

Assessment of applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicant will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. 

Applications that are incomplete with regards to the above requirements will not be assessed by the committee. Shortlisting and tests may be used in the assessment process and references may be obtained. 

About SDU
SDU is committed to fostering a diverse staff that reflects society’s diversity. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background.
SDU was founded in 1966 and now has over 27,000 students, nearly 20% of whom are international. SDU employs more than 3,800 staff and offers 115 study programmes across disciplines such as the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, health sciences, and engineering. While SDU’s main campus is in Odense, it also has campuses in other locations.

Equal opportunity employment
The University of Southern Denmark is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, or any other protected status.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes our staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, are subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position.

How to apply
Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now" on our website.

We recommend reading "How to apply for a position at SDU" before applying.

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

 

Application deadline: November 23, 2026, 23:59 CET/CEST.

 

Applicants may also wish to consider the related Postdoc positions ‘Hybrid War and Democracy’ at The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS). Candidates interested in both positions must submit a separate application for each position, as appointment to a position is only possible if an application has been submitted for that specific vacancy.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc positions ‘Hybrid War and Democracy’ at The Danish Institute for Advanced Study DIAS
jobs.description:
The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) at the University of Southern Denmark, Odense, invites applications for one or more full-time Postdoc positions.

The ’Hybrid War and Democracy’ initiative explores changes in how international conflicts are waged. Domestic and foreign influence campaigns are bolstered by new digital technologies and artificial intelligence. This creates new challenges for democracies, threat perceptions, information integrity, and for citizens’ information agency.

The postdoc positions will be part of a broader initiative understanding these new dynamics. 

Employment is expected to begin on April 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter, and will be for a period of up to two years. The place of employment will be Odense.

Research profiles and tasks

We are looking for a candidate with a background in computational social sciences, data science, including (but not limited to) computer science, communication, political science, linguistics, information studies, digital humanities, sociology or psychology. 

An ideal candidate would have a strong interest in the topic and bring methodological skills to conduct cutting edge work in this space. The Postdoc(s) will be embedded in an interdisciplinary project team and collaborate closely with other scholars at DIAS and the Centre for Digital Democracy.

Candidates must have a research profile grounded in the use of computational methods to answer social science questions. Research within this project will primarily involve using quantitative and computational techniques as well as surveys and/ or experiments.

Expectations and key responsibilities

The Postdoc(s) will be involved in all aspects of the research, from conception, execution, analysis, publishing, and public dissemination. A strong background in computational techniques is necessary, and experience the topic would be ideal.

Candidates are expected to be willing and able to contribute to DIAS and DDC by producing original research of high international quality, engaging in information exchange with both academic and non-academic actors (e.g., journalists, the public, and policy makers), contributing to grant acquisition efforts, and translating technical details across different disciplines.

Candidates are expected to:

• 
Be capable of working independently and on a team through the research process, including with regards to data collection, data analysis, writing scientific articles, and knowledge dissemination.

• 
Be able to translate methodological specifics to non-computational researchers

• 
Contribute both academically and socially to the research environment at DIAS and the DDC

• 
Code proficiently in R or Python.

• 
Be able to communicate project results in English both in writing in academic contexts and to the broader public (Danish would be an advantage but not required)

• 
Present research results at international conferences in social science or computational disciplines

• 
Possibly contribute to teaching programs (in consultation with relevant departments)

• 
Work and be present in Odense

Inquiries about the project and the positions can be addressed to Prof. Claes de Vreese (chv@sam.sdu.dk). 

About The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally. 

About the DDC

The DDC is a part of the Faculty of Business and Social Sciences. It is an interdisciplinary Centre with members from computer science, law, media studies, political science, business, and organizations. The DDC believes in fostering a stimulating and inspiring environment for both faculty members and students. The DDC’s ambition is to recruit, develop, and retain talented scholars committed to both research, education, and impact. Furthermore, the DDC wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. Among other things, the staff answers questions concerning salary, taxation, housing and accompanying family. Additional information about working in Denmark can be found at Work in Denmark.

Application and assessment process

Appointment to the position requires a PhD degree or equivalent and will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the Danish state with the associated circular on the protocol on job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for the position of postdocs as described herein.

An application must include:

• 
A cover letter stating your specific interest and qualifications for the project in question (max two pages). It is strongly encouraged that you include a github link or proof of coding proficiency. 

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information and date entries

• 
Copies of certificates and diplomas (BSc, MSc, and PhD degrees)

• 
The names and complete contact details (including phone numbers and email addresses) of at least two references

• 
A complete list of publications indicating which publications are most relevant for the position

• 
The 3 most relevant publications or unpublished chapters of the PhD thesis. 
NOTE: If publications have been co-authored, co-author statements must be included and contain information like in this example. The statement is just for your inspiration

• 
A teaching portfolio as documentation for teaching experience (if applicable).

 All non-Danish documents must be translated into English.

Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

Applications that are incomplete may be rejected without any substantive evaluation.

Assessment of applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Applications will be assessed by an academic assessment committee that determines whether applicants are qualified to be a postdoctoral fellow. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. The committee reserves the right to arrive at a decision solely based on the material submitted.

Shortlisting may be used in the assessment process. As part of the assessment, a short coding test may be held.

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. The assessment report will subsequently be forwarded to the Head of Department who will assemble an appointment committee. The appointment committee will manage and complete a series of job interviews with especially promising applicants. On the basis of the applications, the written assessments, the job interviews, and a deliberation within the appointment committee, the head of department determines which candidate(s) will be offered the position.

We recommend reading "How to apply for a position at SDU" before applying.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now" on our website.

Uploaded files must be in Adobe PDF (unlocked). The application and CV must each not exceed 10 MB in file size.

 

Application deadline: November 23, 2026, 23:59 CET/CEST.

 

Applicants may also wish to consider the related DIAS Fellow position in Hybrid War and Democratic Challenges. Candidates interested in both positions must submit a separate application for each position, as appointment to a position is only possible if an application has been submitted for that specific vacancy.

 

Salary and employment terms

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

The Mads Clausen Institute, Center for Nano Optics (www.sdu.dk/nano-optics) invites applications for an Associate Professor position in ‘Experimental Nano-Optics’. The starting date is Feb 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

The successful candidate is expected to conduct cutting-edge experimental research within nano-optics involving advanced optical characterization of localized and propagating strongly enhanced and confined electromagnetic excitations with the state-of-the-art amplitude and phase-resolved near-field microscope available (NeaSpec). The near-field characterization is expected to be complemented with other optical characterization techniques as well as with performing advanced electromagnetic modelling. The candidate should have documented teaching experience at both BSc and MSc levels along with the corresponding teaching portfolio.

The application material should include a detailed motivation and an outline of the research activities that are to be pursued. In their applications, applicants should highlight their ten most significant journal publications, detailing also their author contributions. Applicants who wish to be considered should provide a link to a fully-updated ResearcherID (www.researcherid.com). The application material should also include detailed accounts on supervision and teaching experience.

The prospective candidates should have a Ph.D. degree in physics, preferably within nano-optics, and documented research experience in the aforementioned experimental techniques. They are expected to have a notable international profile, strong record of research publications, and demonstrated exceptional potential to excel in scientific research. We expect the candidate to actively engage in the development of academic research, conducting vigorous fund raising activities, and educational environment at the Centre for Nano Optics.

The candidate is expected to teach and instruct both graduate and undergraduet students as well as supervise bachelor and master projects. Furthermore, the candicate is expected to contribute actively to young-researcher education through supervision of Ph.D. students and postdoctorial researchers. 

For further information about the position and research infrastructure as well as Centre for Nano Optics, contact Prof. Sergey I. Bozhevolnyi (seib@mci.sdu.dk).

jobs.occupation: Position as a doctoral candidate (PhD student) at Department of Clinical Physiology and Nuclear Medicine within Centre of Diagnostic Investigations, Rigshospitalet Copenhagen University Hospital.
jobs.description:
This is a 3-year full-time PhD position with enrollment in the PhD program at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. The successful candidate will contribute to research that seeks to improve the quality, accuracy, and clinical utility of positron emission tomography (PET) imaging using artificial intelligence (AI). Specifically, the PhD project will focus on developing and validating PET emission-derived AI-based attenuation correction methods that enable artifact-free, time-matched attenuation estimates and support ultra-low-dose PET imaging and improved quantitative analysis.

Tasks include:

• You will work at Rigshospitalet, Department of Nuclear Medicine

• You will join the DEPICT AI and image analysis section, and work with our group of computer scientists, engineers, physicists and medical doctors.

• You will join Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network PREFERENCE, including international mentoring and exposure to both academic and industrial research environments.

• You will work with advanced AI models to address PET quantification related to motion artifacts and attenuation correction.

• One-month secondments are planned with University of Bern to work on integration into AI-based reconstruction and with University of Amsterdam to work on repeatability studies with different tracers. A secondment at Siemens Healthineers, Knoxville is planned for reconstruction integration.

Qualifications:

• A master’s degree in computer science, physics, biomedical engineering or equivalent

• Ability to work independently

• "Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English"

• Good programming skills; Python experience is a plus

• Experience with AI development with focus on deep learning and images

• Strong collaboration skills

• Knowledge of medical image data will be an advantage

• Willingness to travel and flexibility

What We Offer

We provide an opportunity to be part of an ambitious research group within a clinical department with focus on state-of-the-art PET/CT scanners utilizing the new and emerging lines of long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) PET/CT’s. The PhD project is fully funded under the EU Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network program, and you will be part of a network of doctoral students working towards developing innovative LAFOV PET/CT image analysis tools and performing groundbreaking clinical LAFOV PET/CT research. You will have a strong supervisor group with both technical and medical background.

The position will be in our new facilities at our AI section, DEPICT, at Rigshospitalet, and you will be referring to Professor Flemming Littrup Andersen at Department of Nuclear Medicine.

General Eligibility Criteria

Mobility Rule: The fellow may not have resided in Denmark, where the research training activities take place, for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to the recruitment date (and may not have carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark).

Early-Stage Researcher: The fellow must be — at the date of recruitment — an ‘early stage researcher’ (i.e. in the first four years (full-time equivalent) of his/her research career and not have a doctoral degree).

Application Process

The application deadline is November 1, 2026, and applications should be submitted online via the job advert link. Applicants are encouraged to submit a CV and a motivated application, detailing relevant coursework, previous research experience, education and practical skills.

We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age, gender, race, religion, or ethnicity.

Terms of Employment

The position is full-time for a period of three years and is available from November 1, 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement within the Capital Region of Denmark. Salary will be negotiated according to the collective agreement for academic personal, see link.

Further information:

PREFERENCE.

Rigshospitalet.

DEPICT.

Project contact: Flemming Littrup Andersen, Clinical Professor, Department of Clinical physiology and Nuclear Medicine.  For further inquiries, please contact Flemming Littrup Andersen (flemming.andersen@regionh.dk) or Claes N. Ladefoged (claes.noehr.ladefoged@regionh.dk)

About Centre of Diagnostic investigation, Rigshospitalet

The Centre of Diagnostic Investigation comprises a collection of highly specialized departments, including Diagnostic Radiology, Clinical Biochemistry, Pathology, Clinical Immunology, Clinical Physiology and Nuclear Medicine, Clinical Microbiology, and Clinical Genetics & Centre of Genomic Medicine.

The centre has approximately 1.550 staff members and an annual turnover of DKK 1.2 billion. Each year, the centre performs approximately 10 million laboratory analyses and 650.000 imaging examinations, based on 1 million contacts with patients and donors.

The centre’s core activities include high-level research, strong educational environments, specialized diagnostics and patient treatment. Its 36 professors and other researchers publish more than 700 scientific articles annually in international journals.

Lead product development that makes a difference - Are you motivated by turning ambitious ideas into robust, manufacturable products that improve people’s lives?

As we strengthen our R&D organization with clearer ownership, deeper functional excellence and stronger cross-functional collaboration, we are looking for an experienced Product Development Project Manager to help shape the next generation of Coloplast solutions.

Join us and take a central role in bringing new products from defined scope to verified, transferable and launch-ready solutions for people living with intimate healthcare needs.

Join Product Development in R&D

You will become part of Product Development within R&D, where mechanical engineering, materials science, systems engineering, test engineering, usability and design collaborate closely across disciplines.

As Product Development Project Manager, you will lead the Product Development workstream within one or more cross-functional development projects or programs. You will translate the agreed project scope into an executable Product Development plan and lead the team in delivering high-quality technical outcomes.

You will represent Product Development in the wider project or program organization and collaborate closely with the overall Project Manager or Program Manager, Product Development line managers, Manufacturing Development, Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, Clinical and Operations.

Your key responsibilities

You will be responsible for creating clarity, structure and momentum across the Product Development workstream.

Your responsibilities will include:

•   Lead the Product Development workstream from early development through design verification, design transfer and launch readiness.

•   Translate the agreed project scope into clear Product Development deliverables, milestones, dependencies and decision points.

•   Establish and maintain the Product Development workstream plan and integrate it with the overall project plan.

•   Build and lead a multidisciplinary team spanning relevant Product Development disciplines.

•   Create clear ownership of deliverables and actively manage workstream risks, issues and critical dependencies.

•   Drive timely decisions within the Product Development mandate, making technical recommendations, assumptions and trade-offs visible.

•   Ensure that Product Development deliverables are completed at the required level of quality and maturity, including relevant product concepts, designs, requirements, specifications, verification evidence and Design Control documentation.

•   Partner closely with Manufacturing Development to integrate product design, Design for Manufacturing and manufacturing-readiness activities from the outset.

•   Forecast resource and OPEX needs, align capacity with Product Development line managers and make resource constraints and consequences transparent.

•   Communicate progress, risks, decisions and recommendations clearly to the project or program organization and other relevant stakeholders.

What you bring

You are a structured and curious project leader who combines disciplined execution with sound judgement and strong collaborative skills.

You do not need to have every technical answer yourself, but you must be able to ask difficult questions, challenge assumptions constructively and help multidisciplinary teams reach well-founded decisions. You are comfortable working with uncertainty while maintaining clarity, accountability and momentum.

We expect that you have:

•   At least five years of experience leading technical or product-development projects in an R&D environment.

•   A master’s or bachelor’s degree in engineering, materials science, design, innovation or another relevant technical discipline.

•   Demonstrated experience leading a technical workstream or multidisciplinary development team.

•   Experience taking products or technical solutions through concept development, detailed development, verification and transfer into manufacturing.

•   Strong capabilities in project planning, risk management, dependency management and stakeholder communication.

•   The ability to make and communicate trade-offs across product performance, quality, manufacturability, sustainability, time and cost.

•   The ability to distinguish between decisions that can be made within the team’s mandate and issues that require broader alignment or escalation.

•   Fluency in written and spoken English.

Experience from medical devices, pharmaceuticals or another regulated industry is strongly preferred. Experience with Design Control, product verification or manufacturing transfer will be considered an advantage.

What we offer

•   A central role in developing products and solutions that make a meaningful difference for people living with intimate healthcare needs.

•   Meaningful accountability for leading technical Product Development execution.

•   Close collaboration with experienced specialists, project managers and leaders across R&D and the wider organization.

•   A strong project-management community across product innovation, technology, Product Development and Manufacturing Development.

•   Opportunities for professional growth within project management, senior project management, program management or functional leadership.

•   The opportunity to help strengthen how Product Development plans, collaborates, decides and delivers.

•   An inclusive culture where different experiences and perspectives are valued and where we make sure that you can be you.

Interested?

If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Majk Kruszewski, Senior Director, Product Development,dkmkru@coloplast.com

About Electricity Maps

Electricity Maps is a VC-backed climate and energy tech start-up building the world's most comprehensive electricity data platform. We provide real-time, historical, and forecasted data on electricity systems worldwide - covering generation mix, electricity prices, carbon intensity, and renewable share.

Our data powers decisions across sustainability and energy markets: from companies like Google and Cisco optimising compute workloads and reporting emissions, to energy market participants using our forecasts to inform trading strategies and asset optimisation. We're a small, technical team based in Copenhagen, working at the intersection of energy, AI, climate change, and data.

About the role

You'll work in the product team responsible for exposing our data to the world and you will help people and companies consume our data: Via our API, our map or whatever makes sense next.

We believe in engineers owning product decisions. Engineers scope the problem, build it and evolve it based on feedback from customers, colleagues and users. Those decisions usually aren't mapped out before you start on them so you're figuring out the shape of the problem and the best solution as you unpack it.

You'll be part of a small engineering team with 3 other full-stack engineers. No two days look the same. Most of your energy goes into building and figuring out solutions, with bug fixes and other tasks mixed in.

What you'll do

• 
Build and ship across the stack (we’re using TypeScript for 95% of the product surface).

• 
Own the systems that touch customers directly, from how we onboard, guide and support them to how we serve data in the API they integrate with.

• 
Decide what to build in collaboration with leadership, sales, marketing and data teams.

• 
Care about your solutions being actually used and understand what matters to our users: dig deeper in analytics, join commercial conversations, be curious.

• 
Push on new ways customers can interact with our data. Maybe new API capabilities, new functionality in the map or something else.

• 
Dig into bugs and edge cases.

What you won't do

• 
Ship something and never find out if anyone uses it.

• 
Wait around for permission to fix something you can see is broken.

• 
Spend more time in alignment meetings than building.

What we're looking for

• 
6+ years of hands-on experience shipping full-stack features in production and scaling them.

• 
Early-stage tech company / product experience.

• 
Product mindset, meaning that you build with the user in mind and have strong, defensible opinions on what "good" looks like; in code, in product, in process.

• 
Comfortable with data-heavy products, where edge cases and correctness can play a big part.

• 
Founder mentality, meaning that you are excited about building new products and taking them from an early stage to something users rely on. You spend time across the organization to deepen your knowledge and learn how users interact with the product to build things that are used.

Our stack

Relevant to this role: TypeScript, Node.js, React, GCP. The ideal candidate has worked in or close to these systems.

The details

Location: Copenhagen (office first, with flexibility)

Type: Full-time

Compensation: Competitive salary + stock options

Benefits: 6 weeks vacation, health insurance, annual company offsite, lunch and snacks at the office

Electricity Maps provides real-time, historical, and forecasted electricity data - including carbon intensity, electricity mix, and prices - for more than 350 regions worldwide. We help businesses cut emissions with confidence, and enable products and services to differentiate by giving end-users the tools to be carbon-aware. We also serve power markets directly: energy traders and market participants use our forecasts to anticipate prices and grid conditions ahead of time. Wind and solar output fluctuates throughout the day, so this data has to be dynamic and updated in real time. And because claims about the physical origin of electricity get scrutinized and challenged, the effort behind it has to be collaborative, open, and transparent - otherwise it's just another unverifiable "100% renewable" claim. That's what motivated Electricity Maps. It started as an open-source real-time visualization in June 2016, founded by Olivier Corradi, and has grown into a comprehensive data platform trusted by companies like Google, Cisco, and Schneider Electric to hit their climate goals and help their users take real, grid-grounded climate action. Our mission: to decarbonise electricity, by building and continuing to build the world's most comprehensive, granular, and useful electricity data platform.

jobs.occupation: Assistant or Senior | Banking & Insurance Audit & Assurance
jobs.description:
Company Description

With more than 8,000 employees, Deloitte is one of the largest professional services firms across the Nordics. We help clients navigate complex business and technology transformations by combining deep industry expertise with leading capabilities in Audit, Tax, Advisory, and Consulting.

Are you passionate about the financial services sector and ready to contribute to high-quality audits in one of the most complex, dynamic and highly regulated industries? We are looking for talented audit professionals to join our Banking & Insurance team in Deloitte Denmark.

We serve a broad range of clients, from major Nordic banks and insurance companies to specialised financial services providers. Our work combines strong audit quality, deep sector knowledge and close collaboration as we help clients navigate complex financial reporting, regulatory and risk-related requirements.

Our Audit & Assurance Banking & Insurance practice brings together approximately 35 professionals. You will join an environment where quality and professional development come first, supported by structured learning, mentorship and exposure to challenging, real-world assignments. We value collaboration, different perspectives and an inclusive culture where people can contribute authentically and develop their careers.

Whether you aspire to become a state-authorised public accountant, deepen your expertise within banking or insurance, or build a broader profile combining audit and advisory experience, we will support your development. Join a community committed to continuous learning and creating lasting value for financial institutions across the Nordics.

Job Description

As an Assistant or Senior in our Banking & Insurance practice, you will play a central role in delivering high-quality audit and assurance services to commercial banks, investment banks, insurance companies and other regulated financial institutions across the Nordics.

Your responsibilities will span the audit lifecycle, from planning and risk assessment to execution and reporting. Depending on your experience level, you will either contribute to defined audit areas with support from experienced colleagues or take broader ownership of workstreams, client interactions and the development of junior team members. Your work will focus on financial reporting, regulatory requirements, operational risks and emerging topics such as cybersecurity, data and digital transformation.

The position is based in our Copenhagen office. Your work will include time at client locations.

In this role, you will

• Own audit workstreams appropriate to your experience level, demonstrating initiative and sound judgement in complex situations.

• Contribute to consistently high audit quality by applying professional scepticism, robust methodology and attention to detail.

• Develop deep sector knowledge of banking and insurance, including the regulatory frameworks, business models and risk profiles that shape these industries.

• Build trusted relationships with clients and colleagues through professionalism, reliability and a genuine interest in their success.

• Use analytical tools and data-driven approaches to identify relevant risks, patterns and insights.

• Mentor and support junior team members, contributing to a culture of continuous improvement and knowledge sharing.

• Use data analytics, automation and AI-enabled tools to support risk assessment, test relevant populations and identify patterns, anomalies and risk indicators that require further audit attention.

You will work in a collaborative environment where your voice is heard, your development is prioritised and your contributions influence how we serve our clients.

Qualifications

You hold a master's degree in accounting, auditing or a related field, or you are actively pursuing such a qualification.

What we're looking for:

• 2–6 years of audit experience, with a demonstrated ability to take ownership of assignments and drive progress.

• A strong analytical mindset: You are curious about how things work, comfortable with data and numbers, and able to identify patterns and anomalies.

• Risk-oriented thinking: You understand that audit is fundamentally about risk assessment and can apply this perspective to complex business scenarios.

• Clear communication: You can explain complex financial and regulatory topics to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Fluent Danish: You can communicate confidently in Danish, both verbally and in writing, as you will work with Danish clients and documentation. This is a requirement for the role.

• Strong English skills: You can work effectively in English, both verbally and in writing, as English is our firm language.

• A genuine interest in people: You listen actively, support colleagues and recognise the value of diverse teams.

• A commitment to growth: You are eager to deepen your expertise, learn from experienced professionals and support the development of others.

Even if you do not meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply if you believe you can contribute meaningfully to our team.

What we offer:

• Continuous learning and development: Access to technical training, sector-specific workshops, professional development programmes and support from experienced colleagues.

• Exposure to leading financial institutions: Opportunities to understand how the Nordic banking and insurance sectors operate.

• Structured mentorship: Guidance from experienced partners and senior colleagues who are invested in your development.

• Flexibility and autonomy: Trust and support to manage your work within flexible working arrangements.

• A vibrant community: A team that values professional connection as well as social activities and events.

• Career pathways: Support whether your ambition is state authorisation, leadership, sector specialisation or a broader audit and advisory profile.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your application, CV, a brief cover letter outlining your interest in banking and insurance audit and assurance work. We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Please do not hesitate to contact Contact Kristian Ehrenreich Hansen, Partner, or Lica Lyngsø Møller, Partner. They would be happy to discuss the role and our Banking & Insurance team.

At Deloitte, we value different skills, perspectives, and experiences, as it enables us to effectively solve complex challenges for our clients. We encourage you to apply for the position if you believe your skills can contribute to our team´s success.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

We are extra[not]ordinary

*(ex· tra· not· or· di· nary |\ ik-ˈstr-not-ȯr-də-ˌner-ē)

Adjective: A unique word for Genmab meaning to go way beyond what is

usual; to be remarkable; proudly unique and authentic

Back to search results

Previous job Next job

JOB DESCRIPTION

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

The Role

The Senior Manager, Quality Global Affiliates Excellence, develops and owns selected shared Quality processes that enable Genmab’s affiliates to operate compliantly and efficiently as the business expands. The role simplifies ways of working, reduces duplication and affiliate workload, and builds scalable solutions that can be deployed across existing and new markets.

Working closely with affiliate Quality leads, global process owners and cross-functional partners, the role combines process ownership with hands-on implementation. A key responsibility is ownership of the affiliate training framework, including shared curricula, governance and ongoing maintenance. The scope of other process ownership is agreed with the Head of Quality Global Affiliates and relevant global process owners, with clear interfaces to local responsibilities.

The role serves as a key connection point between Global Quality and affiliate Quality organizations, coordinating implementation activities, promoting standardization, and enabling the exchange of best practices and lessons learned across markets.

Responsibilities

Affiliate QMS and launch readiness

• Support new affiliate establishment, onboarding of local Quality leads and Responsible Persons, and implementation of the global Quality Management System. Work with local experts to identify and address additional local requirements

• Coordinate Quality readiness activities for market entry and commercial launches, tracking dependencies, milestones and risks and escalating issues requiring decisions or additional resources

• Support inspection readiness through shared tools, knowledge exchange and follow-up on recurring findings and improvement opportunities

Process ownership and scalable ways of working

• Own the design, implementation, maintenance and continuous improvement of assigned affiliate processes, including procedures, tools, governance, performance measures and user support

• Review affiliate workflows with local Quality leads to identify duplication, unnecessary complexity and activities that can be managed centrally or through shared services. Prioritise improvements based on compliance risk, affiliate effort and business needs

• Move agreed repeatable activities into shared solutions with clear responsibilities, handovers and support arrangements, reducing the need for each affiliate to develop and maintain its own approach

• Partner with global process owners to make global Quality processes practical for affiliates. Establish a common core with justified local adaptations, preserving local Quality oversight and statutory responsibilities

Affiliate training framework

• Own and maintain the affiliate training framework in partnership with Global Training, including role and task curricula, assignment principles, onboarding pathways and change governance

• Lead the affiliate training coordinator network and coordinate consistent implementation across markets. Maintain shared training matrices and coordinate updates following changes to global procedures

• Establish efficient arrangements for training assignment, administration and reporting with Global Training and affiliate coordinators. Retain clear local responsibility for identifying local requirements and confirming role applicability

• Monitor training completion and effectiveness, address recurring gaps with relevant stakeholders, and simplify training requirements and administration where justified

Quality oversight and continuous improvement

• Streamline affiliate Quality Management Reviews through common inputs, reporting and follow-up tools, and facilitate Quality Risk Management activities across affiliates

• Use process performance, affiliate feedback, inspection findings and workload data to identify improvements. Measure benefits through reduced duplication and effort, timely implementation and sustained process effectiveness

• Partner with relevant system owners to introduce proportionate digitalisation and automation

Project delivery and capability building

• Lead cross-functional improvement projects from problem definition through implementation and benefit evaluation, managing priorities and dependencies across multiple affiliates

• Build stakeholder commitment, provide practical guidance and training, and follow through on adoption so that improvements become part of everyday work

• Capture and share best practices and lessons learned through reusable guidance, peer networks and onboarding materials, strengthening the capabilities of small affiliate Quality teams

Requirements

• Master’s degree in pharmacy, life sciences, engineering or a related scientific discipline

• Approximately 7–10 years of relevant Quality experience within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry

• Strong understanding of Good Distribution Practice and other GxP requirements relevant to affiliate operations, with experience implementing or improving Quality Management Systems

• Demonstrated experience owning or substantially improving processes across multiple markets or functions, with measurable gains in simplicity, efficiency or effectiveness

• Experience with Quality Risk Management and inspection readiness, including the ability to coordinate these activities across multiple markets

• Experience developing and implementing Quality guidance, tools, and training to enable structured, consistent, and scalable ways of working across affiliates

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and process-improvement capabilities, with the ability to identify trends, simplify processes, and drive harmonization across markets with differing regulatory requirements

• Strong stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across global and local organizations and drive outcomes without direct authority

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK666.400,00---999.600,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

About Genmab

Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).
